gate_results.question: Is the FEC dielectric constant 78.4 traceable to an actual measurement, and at what temperature?
gate_results.answer: Yes. Kobayashi, Inoguchi, Iida, Tanioka, Kumase & Fukai, J. Fluorine Chem. 2003, 120(2), 105-110, DOI 10.1016/S0022-1139(02)00317-2, Table 2 'Physical properties of non-fluorinated and fluorinated carbonates', third data row reads verbatim: 210 17.3 1497 4.1e 78.4e 1.04e Our data. The dielectric entry carries footnote marker e, and Table 2 footnote e reads 'At 23 C.'. Table 2 footnote b reads 'Physical properties are cited from ref. [11,12] except our data.', so this row is the authors' own measurement and not a compilation of someone else's number.
gate_results.identification_basis: Flamme 2017 Table 1 entry 21 reads mp 17.3 / bp 210 / viscosity 4.1 / dielectric 78.4. The same table's entry 20 is ethylene carbonate (eps 89.8), entry 22 is propylene carbonate (eps 64.9) and entry 26 is vinylene carbonate (mp 22, bp 162, eps 126.0), which fixes the entry numbering. The Kobayashi 2003 Table 2 row carries the same four numbers and is marked 'Our data'. Note that the Kobayashi table's compound-name column is a structure graphic that does not survive text extraction, so the mapping to FEC rests on this fingerprint match plus the entry numbering, not on a text label inside the row.
gate_results.citation_chain: ECW-308 Table S3 entry 166 (78.40) -> Flamme 2017 Table 1 entry 21 (78.4, refs [36],[42]) -> [42] Kobayashi 2003 Table 2 (78.4, 'Our data', 23 C)
gate_results.round4_correction: Round 4 recorded, correctly, that Flamme 2017 was not established as the FEC 78.4 primary measurement because RSC answered 403 and its table could not be read. What round 5 adds is the next layer rather than a reversal: Flamme's Table 1 entry 21 does carry the value 78.4, and the body text states it explicitly, but Flamme is a compilation. It is a bearer of the number and still not the measurement. The only part of the round-4 wording that has to be retired is the impression that Flamme does not carry the value at all.
gate_results.temperature_boundary: The canonical row stores 298.15 K; the primary measurement is at 23 C = 296.15 K, a 2.0 K difference. It stays inside the stored row's room_temperature band, but it is not the same temperature and is recorded rather than rounded away. This is a stand-alone note: FEC has no restricted capture, so the crosscheck probe's 5 K comparison window does not apply to it.

gate_results.question: Is the FEC 107 leg readable at primary level?
gate_results.answer: No. Hagiyama et al., Chem. Lett. 2008, 37(2), 210-211, DOI 10.1246/cl.2008.210 resolves to an OUP article page behind a Cloudflare 403; J-STAGE redirects to its 404 page; Unpaywall, CORE, Europe PMC and OpenAIRE all report closed. The accessible abstract states that the relative permittivities of FEC were measured as a function of temperature but carries no number. Ue et al. 2014, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-0302-3_2, is behind Springer identity authorisation.
gate_results.honest_boundary: Not read is not the same as not existing. The earlier transcription of Ue Table 2.3 remains a previously recorded manual observation and is not re-derived this round.

gate_results.question: Is the vinylene-carbonate dielectric constant of 126 traceable to an actual measurement, and at what temperature?
gate_results.answer: Yes. Saadi & Lee, J. Chem. Soc. B: Physical Organic, 1966, pp. 5-6, DOI 10.1039/j29660000005. The Experimental section states that calibration of the dielectric cell against benzene, methanol and water gave a linear capacity-dielectric-constant plot, and that extrapolation of that line to the capacity of the cell filled with vinylene carbonate gave E (25 degrees) = 126 +/- 1.0. Table 2, 'Physical properties of some cyclic carbonates at 25 C', lists vinylene carbonate as dielectric constant 126, dipole moment 4.45 D, density 1.81 and boiling point 162 C. The abstract states the dielectric constant and dipole moment were measured.
gate_results.method: Brass dielectric cell to a Wissenschaftlich-Technische Werkstaetten design, oscillator and measuring technique after Few, Smith & Witten, calibrated against benzene, methanol and water.
gate_results.identifier_confirmation: This also settles the round-4 identifier question. DOI 10.1039/j29660000005 is a vinylene-carbonate paper, not a nitrile paper, and Reaxys pins the same citation to the vinylene-carbonate substance row. The repository's earlier naming of it as an adiponitrile/glutaronitrile ticket was the error.
gate_results.dataset_consequence: The canonical row stores dielectric 126 at T_K 298.0. The primary measurement is 126 +/- 1.0 at 25 C = 298.15 K, so the stored number is confirmed and the 0.15 K temperature difference is within the reporting precision of the source. The row's evidence_level and conflict_status are therefore stale and are specified for revision in the backlog.

propylene_carbonate.note: no footnote marker; the canonical row stores 64.9 at 298.15 K from Simeral (1970)

ethylene_carbonate.note: asterisked as measured at 40 C; the canonical row stores 90.5 at 313.15 K from Chernyak (2006)

artifact.access_route: article PDF supplied by the user from an institutional session

second_source_corroboration.detail: mp 22 / bp 162 / dielectric 126.0 / dipole 4.45, i.e. the same vinylene-carbonate constants as Saadi & Lee. Flamme is a compilation citing [46],[47]; [47] is Saadi & Lee 1966, i.e. the SAME primary source, so this is same-source repetition rather than independent corroboration, and it does not raise the evidence level.

gate_results.question: What does the licensed index itself expose for the vinylene-carbonate dielectric constant?
gate_results.answer: In Reaxys the substance vinylene carbonate (CAS 872-36-6, Reaxys registry number 105683, 59 physical-data entries) carries the category 'Dielectric Constant - 1'. The record's table has six columns: Dielectric Constant, Frequency (Dielectric Constant) Hz, Temperature (Dielectric Constant) C, Location, Comment (Dielectric Constant), Reference. The single data row leaves all five data columns empty and populates only Reference, which reads 'Saadi; Lee / Journal of the Chemical Society B: Physical Organic, 1966, p. 5'. The index therefore confirmed that a measurement exists, and where it was published, but carried no numeric value.
gate_results.reaxys_full_text_route: The row's 'Full Text' button opened pubs.rsc.org/j2/article/266593. The page passed a bot interstitial and redirected to an institutional SSO login. The Royal Society of Chemistry is not in the institution's entitlement (user-confirmed), which is why the number had to come from the PDF the user supplied instead.

gate_results.question: Does a licensed index carry a dielectric constant for 3-methoxypropionitrile?
gate_results.answer: No. Reaxys holds 3-methoxypropionitrile (CAS 110-67-8, Reaxys registry number 1739284) with 103 physical-data entries. Its property-category list contains no 'Dielectric Constant' entry; the only electrical quantity present is a single 'Electrical Moment'. Ue, Ida & Mori 1994, J. Electrochem. Soc. 141(11), 2989-2996, DOI 10.1149/1.2059270, remains behind IOPscience's paid abstract page.
gate_results.scope_limit: This is a statement about the coverage of one licensed index and about one blocked paper, not a proof that no dielectric measurement of MOPN exists anywhere.
gate_results.consequence: The canonical row keeps evidence_level secondary_compilation_unverified and model_ready false. The negative evidence now has a licensed-index leg to go with the earlier open-source legs.

gate_results.question: For each frozen target, are the restricted SpringerMaterials observations near the stored temperature an independent measurement or a re-publication of the very source the dataset cites?
gate_results.answer: Of the six targets that have at least one restricted capture near the stored temperature, two are same-source confirmations, three are independent-only, and one mixes the two. The distinction changes what the agreement is worth.

same_source_details.meaning: The restricted record cites the identical 2013 paper the dataset row rests on. This confirms transcription, not independent agreement.

mixed_details.meaning: One restricted reference is the dataset's own source; two are older independent measurements.

gate_results.question: Do the stored values that are means of several observations reproduce from the local ThermoML extraction?
gate_results.answer: Yes, where the dataset stores a mean the local observation-level extraction reproduces it.

gate_results.question: Are pressure-series observations kept out of the ambient-pressure comparison?
gate_results.answer: Yes. The round enforces an ambient window of 90 to 110 kPa. N-methylpyrrolidone is the only target affected: its Uosaki 1996 series runs from 100 kPa to 250 MPa, and the generator kept the 5 near-room rows that sit inside the ambient window while counting 5 pressurised rows as excluded. No pressurised value entered any comparison.

gate_results.question: Which frozen targets exist in the restricted catalog index but carry no captured values?
gate_results.answer: Four: ethylene carbonate (SMI_SC_31657), gamma-valerolactone (SMI_SC_31853), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (SMI_SC_31827) and sulfolane (SMI_SC_31784). Each has a catalog record but zero captured rows near the stored temperature, so no comparison was possible. Six further targets have no catalog record at all: 3-methoxypropionitrile, vinylene carbonate, fluoroethylene carbonate, 2,5,8,11-tetraoxadodecane, propylene carbonate and acetonitrile.
gate_results.note: Catalog presence is metadata only. It is not evidence that a usable value exists, and it is not written as one.

gate_results.question: Can the Materials Project API supply the experimental liquid dielectric constants in scope?
gate_results.answer: No. A silicon-dioxide control returns 200 with total_doc 322 and computed dielectric fields, proving the key and endpoint work, while ethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate and acetonitrile each return 200 with total_doc 0. The dielectric quantities the API exposes (e_total, e_ionic, e_electronic, n) are calculated crystal properties, not measured liquid permittivities, and the summary endpoint silently ignores unrecognised fields such as 'dielectric'.
gate_results.evidence_scope: Six requests to api.materialsproject.org, plus the existing in-repo caches.

gate_results.question: Does NIST Chemistry WebBook carry dielectric data for the targets?
gate_results.answer: No. A case-insensitive full-page search of the 53 cached WebBook files for dielectric, permittivity, epsilon and the epsilon glyph returned zero hits. Thirteen of the fourteen targets resolve to an identity-matched compound page; none carries a dielectric field or a dielectric reference title. A fourteenth fetch for FEC returned 'Registry Number Not Found'.
gate_results.positive_controls: Water, methanol, ethanol and acetone pages were checked the same way and also carry no dielectric field, ruling out a target-only lookup failure.
gate_results.evidence_scope: One new request plus the 53 local caches. This is a statement about the pages examined, not an absolute claim about the whole site.

gate_results.question: Is CatalystHub usable as a data source?
gate_results.answer: No. api.catalysthub.com and catalysthub.com both timed out with no HTTP status. A similarly named reachable domain returned 200 behind a DDoS guard but could not be confirmed to be the same service. The stored API key was read only from the git-ignored config path and was never transmitted to an unconfirmed host.

Closing the FEC 78.4 leg does not resolve the 78.4 versus 107 disagreement and does not make the row model-ready. The canonical FEC row still stores 102, which the repository itself records as the flash point rather than a permittivity; this round documents the fix and does not apply it.
The vinylene-carbonate stored number needs no correction, but the row's evidence_level and conflict_status understate what is now known. That too is documented and not applied.

The SpringerMaterials statements rest on a capture taken on 2026-09-23 under data/restricted/, because both restricted websites (SpringerMaterials and the SIOC database) are currently unreachable. No fresh crawl was made from those two sites this round; the new restricted materials listed below came from other restricted sources (Kobayashi 2003, Saadi & Lee 1966, Reaxys, Flamme 2017).
Same-source confirmation is not independent agreement. The two dinitrile rows share the DOI 10.1021/je300958c with the restricted record and are labelled accordingly.
The Reaxys record for vinylene carbonate carried the citation but no number; that observation is recorded as what the index shows, not as evidence that the number does not exist.
The MOPN negative is scoped to one licensed index and one blocked paper.

Materials Project, NIST WebBook and CatalystHub verdicts are scoped to the requests actually made: three target formulae for Materials Project, 53 cached pages plus one fetch for WebBook, and three entry points for CatalystHub.
No claim is made about compounds outside the frozen 246-row dataset.
